title: Penn State notebook | Matt Campbell discusses his role on game day, embracing history
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
Game day is right around the corner.

With the 2026 season just three days away, Matt Campbell took the podium in the Lasch Building on Wednesday to discuss his role on the team, player positions and embracing history.

Here's a look at what he had to say.

Campbell's role

With Taylor Mouser and D’Anton Lynn calling the offensive and defensive plays, respectively, Campbell shared on Wednesday what his primary role will be on the sidelines, which is mostly monitoring the pace of play.

“I think we go in with a plan of how we assume the game is going to go,” Campbell said. “As we all know, that never goes to plan.”

Among the specific areas Campbell will focus on regarding pace of play is the tempo of the game and situational football.

Through these duties, he’ll utilize analytics to help make decisions on the field — as will the rest of the staff. However, he doesn’t focus solely on analytics, as football is “a people game, a flow game.”

“We use (analytics), but it is not the gold stamp,” Campbell said. “Your job is to find the momentum and the flow of the game that allows you to win the football game.”

While Campbell will focus more on the different management roles, he’ll still help with the occasional playcall and game preparation. Mouser and Lynn, however, will bear the primary responsibilities.

“We got such great coaches that I feel really confident,” Campbell said.

Chess pieces

Since he committed to Penn State in January, safety Jeremiah Cooper has been one of the most anticipated players on the team. However, his recovery from a torn ACL has kept his practice time limited throughout the offseason.

During Campbell's press conference on Tuesday, he said Cooper was probable for Week 1 against Marshall, thus raising a question on Wednesday about his role.

“We have some great chess pieces, guys that can do different things based on the game plan, based on the week,” Campbell said. “He can play corner, he can play nickel, he can play safety.”

While it’s not confirmed whether Cooper will see the field on Saturday, Campbell expressed his confidence in Cooper’s overall ability to line up anywhere he’s put.

Campbell also discussed cornerback Zion Tracy sharing a similar role, who he’s previously described as “one of the best football players he has ever coached.”

“I think finding what fits isn’t even going to be certain for Week 1,” Campbell said. “I think for us, it’s really based week-to-week on where we can play him and where he fits in.”

Embracing history

Campbell brought in Sue Paterno less than a week ago, the wife of late coach Joe Paterno, to speak with the team. She was also invited to Victory Day last Friday.

On Tuesday, Penn State Athletics announced the Paterno Family Football Experience Room in the All-Sports Museum.

“I just feel like to me, coming in here, understanding that (history) is the superpower of Penn State,” Campbell said. “These are the people with their blood, their sweat, their tears, their time, their effort. They built this opportunity for us to be able to grow forward.”

Campbell has prioritized connecting the current roster — many of whom are new to Penn State — with former players and icons of the program. He’s hired lettermen Lynn and Michael Mauti to his staff and brought in dozens of alumni to speak to the team over the summer.

“I think from my end of it, it means the world to me to understand our history, to understand our past and to make sure our young men in our program understand the history and past of Penn State football,” Campbell said.

title: Agostino Abbatiello granted $250,000 secured bail
author: Mia Debelevich | Managing Editor
description:
Agostino Abbatiello was granted $250,000 secured bail by Centre County Common Pleas Judge Jonathan D. Grine during his preliminary hearing on Wednesday morning.

Philip Masorti, Abbatiello's lawyer, argued that Abbatiello is not a flight risk nor a danger to the community. Masorti requested $200,000 unsecured bail.

The bail conditions include Abbatiello residing in his parents' house, not consuming alcohol or drugs, surrendering his passport and not contacting witnesses. His parents will have to transport him to and from court proceedings.

Abbatiello is one of two alleged leaders in a cocaine-trafficking ring involving several Penn State fraternities. He was affiliated with the Sigma Chi fraternity while he was a student.

Megan McGoron, a prosecutor with the Attorney General's office, asked for Abbatiello's bail to either be denied or set at $5 million.

"It wasn't until his face was plastered on national news that he decided to turn himself in," McGorgon said.

Abbatiello had previously been denied bail.

title: Column | ‘Jane Eyre’ sets us free from conformity
author: Kippi Hall | The Daily Collegian
description:
We’re in the Dark Ages for reading.

This year has shown the lowest literacy rates in high school seniors since 1992, according to a survey done by the Nation’s Report Card. A recent article published by The Atlantic, “The End of Reading is Here,” has taken the internet by storm, signaling a death knell on the classics.

But what could be a better following act to the Dark Ages than a Renaissance?

Fiction has the unique power to make one feel seen, to teach and to connect before they look up from the page. One of these novels with considerable relevance is Charlotte Brontë's “Jane Eyre,” published in 1847.

The titular character, Jane Eyre (pronounced “air”), is anything but a “Plain Jane,” except for the fact that she is on the outside. She and other characters in the book frequently describe Jane as “plain,” or unattractive, but Jane prides herself on her passion, moral fortitude and intellect, often refusing to conform to everyone’s meek expectations of her.

For many college students, the pressure to conform is omnipresent. Combined with the oft-touted chance to reinvent yourself, the temptation of molding yourself into someone more appealing, more agreeable and less “cringe” also looms over campus. Without family and old friends to rein students in, increased chances of risky behavior and peer pressure – conscious or not – grow as we try to belong somewhere new, according to a study from New York University.

Jane, too, struggles with her desire to belong after years of mistreatment, internally begging to be loved for who she is. She wishes she were prettier to gain affection from Mr. Rochester — Jane’s rich, brooding employer — while comparing herself to Blanche Ingram, a wealthy and beautiful but vapid young woman vying for his courtship.

In the wake of social media, comparison of our looks and the grandeur of our lives is constantly in play, often leading us to connect external validation online to our self worth, according to a study from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

However, Jane knows the value of her heart and mind, despite her looks and economic status. She iconically goes on to say to Mr. Rochester: “Do you think, because I am poor, obscure, plain, and little, I am soulless and heartless? You think wrong! — I have as much soul as you — and full as much heart!”

Jane has the chance to be “loved” throughout the story, but turns it down after wrestling with her moral standards. Even though she would finally belong to someone other than herself, it would go against what her heart demanded: true love without surrendering who she was. In the face of adversity, she chose her own beliefs before a love that wasn’t up to her standards, leaving her bereft, impoverished and lonely at times.

Love, particularly validation, can be a potent drug. According to a study from the American Psychological Association, college students who rely on external sources for validation, like academic success, peer approval and personal appearance, show higher rates of stress, anger and even lower grades than those who rely on internal sources. In the same study, students who valued themselves based on internal virtues, like Jane Eyre learns to do, reported better grades, lower stress and higher self esteem.

After a lifetime of rejection from the society around her, Jane developed a resolve that may be useful for those who struggle with craving approval from others: “If all the world hated you and believed you wicked, while your own conscience approved of you and absolved you from guilt, you would not be without friends.”

The varied and often unstable opinions of the world, whether from a classmate or someone at the other end of the bar, have no bearing on who you are. While the feelings of love and belonging from others are vital — humans remain social creatures, after all — the only approval that matters is your own, and the compromise for a half-empty sense of belonging at the expense of who you are isn’t worth it.

In the end, Jane’s courage to find herself and make her own path in the face of immeasurable obstacles and temptation to falter on her beliefs is exactly what has captured readers’ attention since 1847.

“Jane Eyre,” at its core, is about love, and how much we choose to sacrifice for it. Should we conform to others’ expectations of ourselves for validation, or do we let the right people love us on our terms? In Jane’s opinion, we should choose the latter.

title: Finding good eats in our college town
author: Talia Rittenhouse | The Daily Collegian
description:
If you’re new to Penn State life, you’ve likely been frequenting the dining halls and dreading picking up the same few options.

But State College has many restaurants to offer. From places to grab a quick slice of pizza, sandwiches and acai bowls, students are never at a loss for food options.

Now, I’m sure that all of the current freshmen have already heard about Roots Natural Kitchen, Honeygrow and Raising Cane’s, but if you’re looking for something new, check out these good eats.

K2 Roots

K2 Roots has an extensive menu of healthy options, such as smoothies, smoothie bowls, juices, paninis and more.

These items allow students to purchase both savory and sweet options, perfect for breakfast, lunch, dinner or even a mid-day snack.

The current featured items are the “Hailey Bieber smoothie,” Peaches and Creme toast, the Allure juice, the Horseradish Dijon Chicken Panini and much more.

A featured smoothie bowl, and one that’s new to me, is the Brownie Batter Bowl. It contains banana, almond butter, agave, cacao, dates, strawberries and other ingredients, all coming together to create the flavors of everyone’s favorite childhood snack: brownie batter right from the mixing bowl.

The Corner Room

While some freshmen may have seen this restaurant on their walks downtown, they may not realize all it has to offer.

The Corner Room isn’t just a place for lunch or dinner, but for breakfast, too. You can get “The Original” Grilled Stickie Bun as a treat, avocado toast, a classic bacon, egg and cheese sandwich or a sweet serving of stuffed french toast.

These options are great for all students, as the food is spectacular, and it aligns with the typical college student budget. Purchases here range from as cheap as $5 to over $20.

If you’re looking for a place to grab food with your friends without your bank account taking a hit, the Corner Room is a great spot to grab a meal.

Pump Station Cafe

The Pump Station Cafe is a short drive out into Boalsburg, so if you don’t have a car, it's time to convince your friends who do with this menu.

The cafe has a wide selection, selling both seasonal featured beverages and its own classics, as well as sweet and savory breakfasts and lunches.

If you follow a gluten-free diet, they also have options here with their baked goods and bread that you can supplement into your orders.

Another fun feature to their menu is their lotus drinks. Personally, I had never heard about this until going to the cafe, but I was pleasantly surprised. A lotus refresher is an energy drink, naturally caffeinated, tasting similar to a flavored tea or lemonade, depending on the flavor you buy.

Whether you love coffee or not, this restaurant is still a great place to go, as it has options for all — caffeine tooth or not.

The Field Burger and Tap

The Field Burger and Tap on 1 Country Club Ln offers more than what may seem. Burgers are a fan-favorite here, but they also serve breakfast and lunch, including pancakes, omelets, salads and appetizers to share.

This one is another quick drive out of downtown, but it’s worth the gas money if you’re looking for a feel-good meal, like the ones you have at home for a barbeque.

There are burgers and sandwiches here influenced by some Penn State coaches, in addition to their staple options, such as “Coach Campbell's Roman Burger” and “Coach Katie's Craft” — you can see what their picks are at the Field Burger and Tap.

And don’t forget to save room for dessert: You can get a milkshake, cobbler, lava cake or another sweet treat to end your meal.

title: Position preview | Penn State WR room has chance to rewrite the narrative
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
For the past few years, Penn State has been known for its struggling wide receivers, and last year’s additions of Trebor Peña, Devonte Ross and Kyron Hudson continued that trend.

This year, the Nittany Lions have several new weapons on offense in Iowa State transfers Chase Sowell and Brett Eskildsen, as well as the highly anticipated return of Koby Howard.

Between those three and many more players, here’s a look at Penn State’s wide receivers this year.

Starters

Sowell and Eskildsen followed Matt Campbell to Happy Valley after spending just one year together at Iowa State.

While being two years younger than Sowell, Eskildsen led the duo with 526 receiving yards, averaging 17.5 yards per catch.

Eskildsen recorded five touchdowns last season, but has the opportunity to add to that mark this season as the Z receiver. His speed will likely play a big role in that, as Campbell said at local media day that he’s ran over 23.5 miles per hour.

The junior was later named to Bruce Feldman's College Football's Top 100 Freaks list.

“(It’s) pretty impressive,” Campbell said on Aug. 7. “He’s got really strong hands and he’s got the ability to accelerate down the field vertically.”

At the same time, Sowell possesses his own traits that make him another top option as the X receiver.

The 6-foot-3 receiver brings four years of collegiate experience at a trio of colleges, where he’s racked up 115 receptions for 1,823 yards and six touchdowns.

However, Sowell has been among the numerous Nittany Lions struggling with consistency this offseason, as Campbell discussed at local media day. Sowell has battled that problem by “being on attack mode.”

Howard will take the field as Penn State’s slot receiver in a very anticipated season for the sophomore.

The sophomore had four starts in his true freshman season, playing in an additional five games. He had a few flashes of success, tallying 133 yards on seven receptions.

“Man, the flashes, you saw what (Howard) could do,” Campbell said on Aug. 7. “He’s had a great summer, man. I couldn’t be prouder of what that guy has done to put himself in a position to have a great camp.”

Role players

Outside of Sowell and Eskildsen, Penn State’s wide receiver room is relatively young.

Keith Jones Jr. came to Happy Valley after one year at Grambling State, where he saw some starting experience. Jones started in two games and saw playing time in another 10 contests, recording 32 receptions for 450 yards and five touchdowns.

Redshirt freshmen Karon Brookins and Zay Robinson have very little collegiate experience from their times at Iowa State, but both have received lots of praise over the last several months, including from Taylor Mouser, who said Robinson has been “challenged a lot this spring” and seen success on the field.

Amarion Jackson is among the influx of true freshmen who will likely see ample playing time this season. Despite being the No. 121 receiver in his recruiting class, per 247sports composite, Jackson has been displaying the confidence of an upperclassman on the field.

“Amarion Jackson is a guy that's taken the program by storm since he's got here on a mission,” Mouser said Tuesday.

Depth pieces

Redshirt junior Ethan Black has the most experience of the remaining wide receivers, having spent the last three years at Penn State. He's played in six games throughout his collegiate career and brings track and field speed to the gridiron.

Peter Gonzalez enters the season as a redshirt sophomore, but he hasn't seen the field for Penn State after redshirting his freshman year and sustaining an injury in Year 2. However, Mouser said on Tuesday that he's one of the players he's seen a lot from this offseason.

The Nittany Lions have several additional faces at wide receiver, including Logan Cunningham, Lyrick Samuel, Max Heffner, Ben Whitver and Hank Hustig, although none of them bring much, if any, collegiate experience.

title: QB Rocco Becht’s leadership sets standard at Penn State by ‘guiding, uplifting and yet always working’
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
When Rocco Becht was a junior in high school, he approached his father, 12-year NFL veteran Anthony Becht, and asked, “What does it take to be the best?”

Becht had already been throwing the football at an elite level since his early days in flag football, but when he inherited the starting quarterback role at Wiregrass Ranch High School in Wesley Chapel, Florida, he knew sacrifices had to be made to become the quarterback he wanted to be.

Thus came countless hours of training that prepared Becht for college recruiting. Mental coaching was a part of that, and he developed strong habits that reinforced his determination. By getting up early, watching extra film and throwing more passes, he made it known he was putting in the work.

“That is the standard — there is no other way to do this,” Anthony told The Daily Collegian. “Young receivers, other quarterbacks, they see that the example is set at the highest level. I can almost promise you that if you ask any of his teammates, they're gonna say, ‘Man, the dude is there always.’ He's always guiding, uplifting and yet always working.”

As Becht enters his first and only season as a Nittany Lion, those traits haven’t left him.

Going hand-in-hand with his ambitious reputation, Becht has been known as a fiery competitor since his childhood. Becht grew up in a house where everything was a competition, and he quickly developed an unquenchable thirst for victory.

“He was super competitive,” Anthony said. “Anything we did — board games, horse, whatever it may be — the loser was gonna be crying at the end of the day.”

Offensive coordinator Taylor Mouser has seen Becht’s competitive flame time and time again at Iowa State and now Penn State. He even took the time to publicly oust Becht as someone who cheats on the golf course because of his desire to win.

“He's got competitive excellence. He's a guy that, until the last second ticks off, you're always going to feel like you have a chance,” Mouser said on Feb. 4. “When you're playing him in the driveway. It's, 'no, next goal wins.' He'll go until he wins.”

Becht was a 3-star recruit out of high school and only had two Power Four offers from Iowa State and Ole Miss. Matt Campbell took a chance on him, and it paid off. He’s now the winningest returning starter in college football and is playing at one of the biggest brands in the country.

“To be able to think of where I am right now at one of the most prestigious, historic programs in college football, I'm super blessed,” Becht said on Tuesday. “This wasn't on my agenda, so now that I am here, I'm super excited to be a part of it.”

In the seasons Becht spent on the bench earlier in his career, he made it a point to study how the starting quarterback acted on and off the field, assessing whether those actions were positive or negative. Through that, he was subconsciously crafting a mental image of what he believed a leader should look like.

When it came time to transition to college football, Becht had the foundational trait required of a team leader: adaptability. He brought his skill at making connections to Iowa State, fostering years-long relationships that carried over to Penn State when many followed Campbell to Happy Valley.

“My leadership style is probably ‘adaptable,’” Becht said at local media day on Aug. 7. “I'm a great connector, in my opinion, no matter where you come from, your background, your history, your ethnicity, your race, I feel like I'm able to connect with everyone. When we go through bad times on the field, I'm able to talk to anyone, lift anyone up.”

It’s his adaptability that’s allowed him to earn the respect of his teammates. Rather than taking the same approach with everyone, he’s learned how to apply specific knowledge about those players to tailor his leadership to them.

“Not everyone's led the same. There will be guys you can get on if you have a closer relationship with them, but there's guys that you have to bring to the side because they may be a hothead and they have to be talked to one-on-one,” Becht said. “Knowing where everyone comes from and knowing their background is huge so that's what I try to do.”

When he arrived in State College, it was a foreign environment he didn’t know too much about before transferring. Becht took it upon himself to introduce himself to every new person he saw in the facility, beginning to build relationships wherever possible.

When Becht decided to transfer to Penn State, he asked general manager Derek Hoodjer for any phone numbers he had to reach out to his new teammates.

At the same time, Becht was dealing with lingering injuries to both of his shoulders that temporarily sidelined him. Although he wasn’t able to work on his craft, Becht established himself as a key leadership figure.

“Rocco's in a completely different space than I've seen him really in his career,” Campbell said Aug. 20. “He's had great command of what we're trying to accomplish offensively, but the biggest thing that a great quarterback does is he leads the team. If the entire locker room is willing to fight for the quarterback, then you got a pretty special leader on your hands.”

Campbell had a pyramid of core values installed on the wall of the Lasch Building meeting room with motivational words that demonstrate the kind of culture he’s trying to build at Penn State. Becht’s teammates have noticed how his growth as a leader closely coincides with many of the emphasized traits, and how he’s leaning into Penn State’s identity.

“Rocco's Rocco at the end of the day,” wide receiver Zay Robinson said. “Rocco's gonna come in and be that leader and be the best teammate every day. You can look at any word on (the pyramid) — loyalty, humility. That man is gritty. He's gonna do whatever it takes for the team to win, no matter what it is.”

Running back Carson Hansen also used the word “gritty” to describe his long-time quarterback, but in a different sense. It’s in the way Becht handles adversity, yet another one of the concepts on the wall, and is something that his father noted as well.

For Becht, everything boils down to his ability to “stay present.” Whether it be at practice, in games or simply spending time with his teammates off of the field, he’s voiced that it’s important for him to focus on what’s happening in front of him.

“You're gonna have bad days, you're gonna have good days, but it's how you bounce back from it,” Becht said. “It's how you stay consistent with it.”

Additionally, Campbell has made clear his philosophy of being “tied at the hip” with his quarterback. He has connected with Becht on a personal level off the field, noting that his faith in himself is what makes him a special player to coach.

Campbell has emphasized the importance of training elite football players. With Becht buying into the core tenets of Campbell’s cultural push, their relationship has only grown at Penn State.

“I believe Penn State football is integrity, character, class, excellence, grit. He embodies every one of those traits,” Campbell said on National Signing Day in February. “He's one of the greatest leaders I've ever been around.”

title: Penn State announces layoffs for WPSU employees, many expected to be hired by WHYY
author: Neel Ved | The Daily Collegian
description:
WPSU employees were notified by Penn State on Monday of layoffs as the station transitions to the ownership of Philadelphia-based WHYY, according to an article from the station.

Many of their employees are expected to transfer to WHYY, with some already receiving job offers, the article said.

The layoffs come after the Penn State Board of Trustees approved the sale of WPSU to WHYY in October 2025. WPSU was originally set to shut down by June 2026, but community efforts led to the sale instead.

According to WPSU, a Penn State spokesperson told the station that the layoffs will affect 31 full-time employees, including 22 staff and nine unionized technical service employees.

WPSU’s transfer is still under consideration by the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). The FCC review will include a 30-day public comment period which will be met on Wednesday. However, there is still no exact timeline for an FCC decision.

“Based on conversation with WHYY and insight from the FCC over the past few months, we believe that the acquisition will be close to complete by mid-September,” the university spokesperson told WPSU.

If the FCC approval takes longer than expected, the university will extend some employees’ contracts so WPSU can proceed throughout the process, the station said.

title: Penn State women's lacrosse earns commitment from midfielder Caitlin McAleenan
author: Gavin Leonard | The Daily Collegian
description:
Class of 2028 midfielder Caitlin McAleenan announced her commitment to Penn State on Instagram on Tuesday.

The Vienna, Virginia native plays for Capital Blue 2028 and attends St. John's College High School.

McAleenan has a proven list of accolades as a junior, including DC All-State First-Team honors and St. John’s College High School Offensive Player of the Year. She is ranked No. 29 in the 2028 class, according to Prep Girls Lacrosse.

McAleenan becomes the first member of Penn State’s 2028 recruiting class.

title: 2 Penn State women's soccer players earn weekly Big Ten awards
author: Rafael Rivera | The Daily Collegian
description:
Three Penn State players received Big Ten weekly honors Tuesday following a week where the Nittany Lions went 2-0 and outscored opponents 11-0.

Redshirt freshman Nicole Crane collected Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week after a seven-point week that included an assist against Bucknell and a hat trick performance against Brown Sunday afternoon, which was the 26th in program history. It was a special set of games for Crane considering it was only her second and third career appearances. The Glen Rock, New Jersey, native has the potential to be a promising scoring threat who can bolster the Nittany Lions attack.

Veteran netminder Mackenzie Gress earned her 2nd career Big Ten Goalkeeper of the Week honors after tallying five saves and two clean sheets against Bucknell and Brown.

Nittany Lion Bella Ayscue was also named a TopDrawerSoccer Team of the Week honorable mention.

title: ‘I’m just adding stuff to my game’ | LB Tony Rojas prepares for Penn State return
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
Tony Rojas last took the field 11 months ago in the White Out game against Oregon. Later that week he tore his ACL, halting what looked like could’ve been a career year for the junior linebacker.

For the next several months, Rojas spent his time rehabbing the injury, eventually returning to the field during summer workouts and fall camp. He also had to learn a new defensive scheme under first-year defensive coordinator D’Anton Lynn.

Now, nearly a full year after his injury, Rojas is set to return to Beaver Stadium against Marshall on Saturday.

“Just being able to be out there with the guys and just play football, play fast, and just have the mentality,” Rojas said Tuesday. “I think it's been great, and I've had a very good camp, and it's been exciting.”

Rojas is arguably the face of Penn State’s defense, and he’s surrounded by a group that brings plenty of experience from Iowa State but less institutional knowledge of the Nittany Lions’ program.

So while he may have been sidelined all spring, Rojas was still a valuable piece of the team as a leader and as a mentor.

“Being a leader this year, my senior year, and having a lot of playing time and just being out here and having wisdom and knowledge for the guys,” Rojas said. “I just feel more of a responsibility of being a leader.”

His experience has also helped him pick up Lynn's defense faster, allowing him to pass along what he’s learned to his teammates who may be having a harder time adjusting to a new scheme.

Rojas has also been sharing what makes Beaver Stadium and playing at Penn State so special, with most of the transfers set to experience it for the first time this Saturday.

“The walk in, warmups, walking out of the tunnel, I think it’s something you have to embrace,” Rojas said. “I think they just need to experience Beaver.”

But Rojas hasn’t spent the offseason focused solely on his role as a leader. He’s also used his time away from the field to improve as a linebacker.

Rojas has always had one of the highest ceilings of any defender at Penn State the last few seasons, but injuries have prevented him from fully reaching it.

As a full-time starter in 2024, he dealt with a lingering injury that required surgery in the offseason. Then when it finally seemed like he was fully breaking out in 2025, he tore his ACL and couldn’t continue living up to expectations.

Now, he has another opportunity to fulfill them.

Throughout his rehabilitation, Rojas studied film of former college football stars, including Sonny Styles, Jacob Rodriguez and Fred Warner, looking for ways to add to his own game.

“I’m just adding stuff to my game,” Rojas said. “I kind of rewatch my film and seeing how I’ve improved and adding stuff to my inventory.”

After nearly a year away, Rojas is finally ready to put those lessons into action. On Saturday, he’ll get his first chance to do so in front of Beaver Stadium.

“I feel like the old Tony,” Rojas said.

MORE FOOTBALL CONTENT

title: Penn State Athletics announces opening of Paterno Family Football Experience Room
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
The history of Penn State football will be on display at the Penn State All-Sports Museum.

Penn State Athletics announced Tuesday the opening of the Paterno Family Football Experience Room to display and recognize over a century of history of football.

The room is headlined by pieces of Joe Paterno's workspace during his 45-year tenure as the Nittany Lions' head coach. Paterno's original office desk and workspace will be on display with a timeline of significant moments from his coaching career at Penn State.

It'll also hold a digital display to recognize the history throughout the years, while also showing off the trophies and individual honors from many of the players over time.

The room will recognize the Hall of Famers, coaches, lettermen and captains, while tapping into the tradition of Penn State with the White Out and football uniforms.

It'll not only serve as a history museum but also display the future of the program under Matt Campbell, who's talked a lot about the buy-in to the tradition that the program has.

Paterno's wife, Sue, recently spoke to the 2026 team in Penn State's team meeting room and was seen at Victory Day on Friday.

The Paterno Family Football Experience Room will open to the public at 10 a.m. Thursday.

title: Former Penn State women's hockey goaltender Katie DeSa inks first PWHL contract
author: Rafael Rivera | The Daily Collegian
description:
Former Penn State goaltender Katie DeSa has signed a 1-year pro contract with the PWHL’s Vancouver Goldeneyes after being selected No. 37 overall.

DeSa was Penn State's anchor in goal, playing all four collegiate seasons for the Nittany Lions. With a total of 85 games, she tallied a program-best 25 career shutouts.

The Pawcatuck, Connecticut, native racked up numerous honors in her collegiate career, such as back-to-back All-AHA First Team selections and back-to-back AHA Goaltender of the Year awards, making her the second player in history to win the award in consecutive years.

DeSa is one of seven Nittany Lions from the 2025 roster to join the PWHL, marking a historic success for the program following the first Frozen Four appearance in Penn State history.

DeSa joins a Vancouver team that has two other goaltenders in Emerance Maschmeyer and Kristen Campbell.

MORE HOCKEY COVERAGE

title: Penn State notebook | Erica Dambach discusses women's soccer team, preparation for nonconference finale
author: Noah Radio | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State wraps up its nonconference schedule on Thursday against Virginia Tech. Ahead of the Hokies’ visit to Happy Valley, head coach Erica Dambach met with the media over Zoom to discuss how her team is progressing as they gear up for conference play.

Shining stars

Before the media session Tuesday, junior defender Bella Ayscue picked up an honorable mention on Top Drawer Soccer’s National Team of the Week after tallying four points in her last two games.

“She is a proper footballer, Bella Ayscue,” Dambach said. “She’s fun to watch, she’s good on both sides of the ball, she did an excellent job against their number 10, who I thought was a really good player for Brown. She’s creative, she’s clever and when you’ve got Molly Martin next to her, you’ve got some freedom.”

Martin is a senior defender who, along with senior goalkeeper Mackenzie Gress, Dambach has gotten a lot out of on the leadership side this season. Dambach also mentioned seniors Kaelyn Wolfe and Kayleigh Herr and junior Aubrey Kulpa as “exceptional” leaders of a team with an adjusting crop of first-year players.

Emergence of first-year players

The Nittany Lions brought in seven players from the high school ranks this offseason, including five four-star recruits. Anna Babcock already started three games, Emma Johnson started two games and Paige Pasinski appeared in all four matchups.

There is also, of course, Ellie Kocher. The highly-touted Allentown, Pennsylvania, native scored her first collegiate goal against Brown on Sunday, and she is beginning to show why she was Soccer Wire’s No. 10 prospect in the nation.

“Well, she’s pretty fun,” Dambach said about Kocher. “Hopefully these other teams have not noticed her yet, but I fear that’s impossible. The coolest thing about Ellie Kocher is that there’s so much more, so much room for her to grow. She is just scratching the surface right now. So now that we’re getting her back in, now it’s about her playing in combination with her fullback and starting to build partnerships with her, and Kulpa, and Crane and all those players.”

Upcoming schedule

Dambach’s squad has been hard at work preparing for both the nonconference finale and the upcoming conference slate. Internally, they have been trying out different lineups and searching for one that sticks.

“We’ve got some players that have played quite well that we’ve rotated out and put others in because we’re just looking at all the different combinations that we have. Obviously, there’s some good firepower in the front six, and so much of that is the way the players combine together and play together,” Dambach said. “We’re really just trying to kind of look at all those different permutations that we can before we get into Big Ten play.”

Before the blue and white travel to Columbus for the Big Ten opener, they have one more nonconference game at Jeffery Field, against Virginia Tech. The undefeated Hokies are led by senior Anna Weir, who has racked up five goals in the young season.

“I think a lot of her success actually has come off of transition; she is really dynamic, so I think first off, kind of stopping it at the root, making sure that when the ball turns over, we’ve got good pressure to win it back,” Dambach said.

Overall, Virginia Tech has a high-energy, momentum-focused style, much like the Nittany Lions.

“They’re off to a hot start, and I think they’ve got a couple forwards that can cause some problems,” Dambach said. “They have primarily been a pressing team with a lot of energy, high energy, high press, and kind of create havoc and turnovers. I think it’s a pretty good side, and I thought they looked quite good against Georgetown.”

The Nittany Lions and Hokies will kick off at Jeffrey Field at 7:30 p.m. on Thursday.

title: Penn State notebook | OC Taylor Mouser talks personnel, importance of Beaver Stadium debut
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Week 1 of the 2026 season is almost here, and offensive coordinator Taylor Mouser took the podium at Beaver Stadium ahead of Penn State’s season-opener against Marshall.

Mouser discussed who’ll be getting meaningful playing time, his relationship with Rocco Becht and what his first game day at Beaver Stadium will look like.

Here’s more of what Mouser said on Tuesday.

Personnel on the field

When asked about which wide receivers he feels comfortable putting in the game, Mouser listed seven players — Chase Sowell, Brett Eskildsen, Koby Howard, Zay Robinson, Amarion Jackson, Keith Jones Jr. and Karon Brookins.

Sowell, Eskildsen and Howard are projected to be the starters, while Mouser believes that the depth will be able to contribute when needed.

“Amarion Jackson is a guy that's taken the program by storm since he's got here on a mission,” Mouser said. “Zay Robinson — I’ve challenged him a lot since this spring. Eskildsen is one of our most consistent guys. Keith, Koby and Karon have done a good job too. That doesn't mean I don't feel good about Peter Gonzalez and some of those other guys. They're veterans and they're trusted.”

Additionally, Mouser claimed that four running backs will play on Saturday and will be routinely used throughout the season. He named Carson Hansen, James Peoples, Quinton Martin Jr. and Cam Wallace.

Each player’s exact usage, Mouser said, is up to running backs coach Savon Huggins, but he has full trust in his colleague to put the right player in the game at the right time, playing to each of their individual strengths.

“All those guys are trusted in my mind,” Mouser said. “We have a million personnel in the offense that we can get to. So, you'll see all four of those guys play. They've all earned the rights to play.”

Mouser also said that Alex Manske has “forced him to play him” through his efforts at fall camp. Although Rocco Becht will be the starting quarterback, Mouser noted that Manske has opened doors for him to design unique run packages.

However, Mouser said that Manske’s biggest improvement has been his consistency in the passing game, something that he credited quarterbacks coach Jake Waters with building.

“He's one of the more impressive looking people, he's gigantic,” Mouser said. “He can run physically as competitive as anybody that we have on the field, and then we really challenged him to grow as a passer.”

Relationship with Becht

Mouser and Becht have been meeting often to talk about the team’s playcalling. He’s had Becht rank the plays he’s come up with and Mouser has put aside the ones Becht doesn’t like.

The communication and teamwork between them is tantamount to how Mouser wants Becht to “play fast and have fun.”

Mouser has given Becht the green light to control the offense on the field, as he knows Becht primarily executes the original playcalls the best he can, but also allows Becht to utilize what he sees in the pocket and do what he feels is best on the fly.

“He trusts what he sees. You can tell there's like another gear to that guy's game,” Mouser said. “I want him to run full speed into it and play his game, play a lot of football, trust the design and make plays.”

Debut at Beaver Stadium

During the Nittany Lions’ fall camp scrimmages, the coaching staff simulated the conditions expected for Saturday. In Mouser’s case, this was being up in the box, as he prefers to be away from the field while working.

“I try to stay as far away from the field as I can when I'm calling it,” Mouser said. “We wanted to get the real operation, what it's going to look like on game day, using the sideline, subbing in people from the personnel standpoint.”

For himself and many of the players, playing at Beaver Stadium will be a different experience than anything they’ve experienced before.

Mouser noted that there’s tremendous value in having these players experience the conditions of playing in front of one of the largest crowds in the world. He’s also curious to see how the team deals with adversity at Beaver Stadium, how the team reacts to failure and who steps up to uplift the team.

“There's a lot of guys on my team that haven't played football in there yet,” Mouser said. “It's going to be an eye-opening experience for all of us, including myself.”

title: Penn State notebook | Matt Campbell reveals starting OL in first game-week press conference
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Matt Campbell took to the podium in Beaver Stadium ahead of his first game as the head coach of Penn State.

The Nittany Lions will face Marshall at 3:30 p.m. Saturday, marking the start of the 2026 season and the beginning of the new era of leadership.

Campbell mentioned his confidence in the quarterbacks, an injury update and the growth of the offensive line in fall camp.

Here’s what Campbell had to say to open his first game week in Happy Valley.

Confidence in the quarterbacks

It may not just be Rocco Becht who’ll see the field on Saturday, as Alex Manske has worked himself into a spot where he will be implemented into the offensive game plan.

Offensive coordinator Taylor Mouser mentioned the talents that Manske brings, and Campbell and Mouser will struggle to keep him off the field.

“As we game plan each week, we try to figure out where he can plug in and where he can give us an advantage in the football game for sure,” Campbell said.

Becht will be one of the most experienced quarterbacks in college football, and that experience under Campbell gives his coaching staff a lot of confidence in him.

“Rocco was never trying to be anybody else but the absolute best version of himself, and I think you've seen that in really critical, hard moments, him step up in key situations and win the football game with the ball in his hand,” Campbell said.

The other aspect of Becht’s game that has taken a jump is his leadership both on and off the field. The quarterback has been one of the key transfers to bridge the gap between the returning players and the former Iowa State coaches on offense.

That leadership has brought the current Penn State team in a position to be ready for game day on Saturday.

“But even greater than the football player is the man and the human being and how he goes through this process to be his best on Saturdays,” Campbell said.

Injury updates

Penn State could be without multiple impact players on Saturday that are still recovering from injuries sustained last season.

Among those, the closest to returning is safety Jeremiah Cooper, who Campbell said is “probable” for the game against Marshall.

“He's probably the closest to being able to play this week,” Campbell said. “He's had a really good week and a half of practice.”

Tight end Gabe Burkle is another key player recovering from a long-term injury after tearing his ACL in November. Campbell said Burkle is “doubtful” for Saturday.

Linebacker Alex Tatsch also went down with an injury later in 2025 and has the same “doubtful” tag for Saturday.

“But all three guys are back on the practice field,” Campbell said. “All three guys are progressing themselves forward. It's just making sure they're absolutely prepared to step back on the field.”

Starting offensive line

Campbell revealed his starting offensive line for Week 1, with multiple position battles having been won up front.

Malachi Goodman won the left tackle job and will start Saturday on Becht’s blindside. Goodman will start alongside Trevor Buhr, Brock Riker, Cooper Cousins and Anthony Donkoh.

Cousins is a player who Campbell said was one of the MVPs of fall camp and is someone who’s consistently put in work on and off the field.

“I think he's physically as dominant as I've seen him, at least from the videotape that I was able to watch a year ago,” Campbell said.

Campbell entered fall camp with a lot of confidence in the group, and the depth behind the starters continues to prove themselves as well.

Behind the starters, Owen Aliciene, Garrett Sexton and Dom Rulli all showed their value as rotational pieces throughout the entire offensive line.

“We feel like there's really good growth there,” Campbell said. “We feel like there's a lot of options, and you know I think it's going to be really exciting to get into the start of the season to see how we rotate guys through.”

title: Position preview | 3 starters headline Penn State’s first TE room under Taylor Mouser
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State is known for its elite tight ends, and the first room under offensive coordinator and tight ends coach Taylor Mouser has the ability to run three experienced players at an elite level.

Here’s a deeper look into Mouser’s debut tight end room at Penn State.

The big three

Of the three projected starting tight ends, two are transfers that followed Matt Campbell from Iowa State — Benjamin Brahmer and Gabe Burkle.

Brahmer is the most decorated tight end on the team, having been one of the Cyclones’ starters for the past three years. He’s coming off a second-team All-Big 12 junior season where he was named a semifinalist for the John Mackey Award, an award given to the nation’s top tight end.

Brahmer had 37 catches for 446 receiving yards and six touchdowns in 12 games.

Burkle was Iowa State’s other starting tight end at many points during the past two years, making 15 starts in 25 career games. He suffered a torn ACL in November, and he’s still progressing through rehab with his status unknown for Week 1.

“He's the guy that cleans up the mess for us on offense,” Mouser said on Aug. 7. “He's the guy that we give the hardest job to. The hardest guy to block — we have Gabe do it. He's the most trusted person that I've probably ever coached. Nobody prepares harder.”

Andrew Rappleyea was the only routinely-used tight end to return to Penn State, with Luke Reynolds transferring to Virginia Tech and Khalil Dinkins off to the NFL. He started in eight of 13 games last season, tallying 20 receptions for 180 yards and three touchdowns.

Rappleyea, like Burkle, missed spring practices due to injury. He also had a season-ending injury as a redshirt freshman in 2024 after starting in the season opener.

Depth pieces

State College native Finn Furmanek has received some meaningful buzz after Campbell noted that he can see the field at fullback. Last season, Furmanek played in all 13 games on special teams.

Cooper Alexander, another transfer from Iowa State, has five catches for 47 yards in 12 appearances across his career, 11 of which were last year. His younger brother, Case, is committed to Penn State in the Class of 2027 as a 4-star linebacker.

“Cooper Alexander to me is a guy that had a really great summer, and physically looks like it can be a matchup issue in some different areas,” Campbell said Aug. 7. “I think that room is certainly healthy at the top end of things, so we're excited about where it's definitely going to be.”

Brian Kortovich — a 3-star in the Class of 2025 — burned his redshirt last season and spent his time on the developmental squad. He was named the Developmental Squad Offensive Player of the Week during the weeks of the Iowa and Michigan State games.

The “new” tight ends

Over the course of the offseason, a few players switched to tight end from other positions.

Bobby Mears originally committed to Penn State as a walk-on wide receiver and linebacker in the Class of 2023. However, he quickly switched to the defensive end when he got to Happy Valley and played the position for three seasons, only appearing in two games. Now, Mears has flipped to tight end.

Jake Lukac, the son of former Penn State tight end Mike Lukac, played at State College Area High School and originally committed as a tight end walk-on. He briefly switched to linebacker for the offseason before going back to tight end.

Peyton Falzone, who was a surprise National Signing Day addition to Penn State’s 2026 class, also recently made the switch to tight end. He was a 4-star and the No. 10 recruit out of Pennsylvania.

“What’s best for him and maybe best for the football team right now was his ability to see what he could do (at tight end),” Campbell said. “We’re really excited about what his future can entail.”

title: Nittany Lions in the NFL | Dani Dennis-Sutton gets first preseason action, WRs make impact
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
The NFL preseason concluded on Saturday, giving players one last chance to earn a roster spot.

Several former Nittany Lions made big plays in Week 3 of the preseason, with one rookie defensive end making the most of his preseason action.

Here’s a look at how former Nittany Lions performed last week.

Sean Clifford, quarterback, Cincinnati Bengals

After throwing his first touchdown as a Bengal last weekend, Sean Clifford found the end zone again this week.

Clifford capped off his fourth NFL preseason by throwing for 53 yards and a touchdown.

The former Nittany Lion peddaled back and found Ke'Shawn Williams for a seven yard strike, who then ran another four yards for the score.

Clifford was listed as No.3 quarterback on the Bengals roster behind Joe Burrow and Joe Flacco during the preseason. However, the Bengals elected to go with just two quarterbacks for the season, sending Clifford to the waivers.

Dani Dennis-Sutton, defensive end, Green Bay Packers

Defensive end Dani Dennis-Sutton earned his first sack in the NFL when he pushed past both Jayden Williams and Matt Pryor on the offensive line before taking down quarterback Gardner Minshew for a 15-yard sack in the first quarter.

After missing a week of practice due to a heat-related illness and Green Bay’s first two preseason games, the former Nittany Lion tallied a pair of tackles, a sack and a tackle for loss in his Packers debut.

Dom DeLuca, linebacker, Baltimore Ravens

Former Penn State walk-on Dom DeLuca was among the best defenders on the field for the Baltimore Ravens in their 41-3 domination against the Washington Commanders on Friday.

DeLuca led the game with eight tackles, five of which were solo tackles.

Baltimore cut former Nittany Lions Nick Dawkins and Adisa Isaac over the weekend and continued that trend with DeLuca’s waiver on Sunday.

Los Angeles Chargers wide receivers

In a nailbiter 20-18 loss against the Los Angeles Rams, a trio of former Nittany Lion wide receivers had huge receptions to keep things close on Thursday.

Liam Clifford led the way with a 24-yard reception from DJ Uiagalelei to work the ball downfield, marking his first reception in the NFL.

KeAndre Lambert-Smith, who’s now in his second year in the NFL, also had a catch for 21 yards. With 22 seconds left in the first half, Uiagalelei found Lambert-Smith to bring the ball past the 50-yard line.

Rookie Devonte Ross only recorded a nine-yard reception, but finished the preseason with five catches for 57 yards and a touchdown.

Clifford and Ross both missed out on the 53-man roster in their first NFL seasons, while Lambert-Smith earned his spot on the team for the second straight season.

title: Didn't get student football tickets? Here's what to do instead.
author: Alli Satterfield | The Daily Collegian
description:
It’s September, and football’s return to Happy Valley is quickly approaching. Now that the rush of the student ticket lottery has settled, some Penn Staters are mourning their lack of student tickets (not me, y’all stay safe though).

While many of us are getting ready to cheer on the Nittany Lions this fall, others won’t be so lucky. Even though some may have better luck next year, they need to fill the time this football season.

Here are my suggestions, as someone who has been in those shoes before.

Walk around the arboretum

I once thought Penn State’s arboretum was overrated. During my freshman year, I felt like everyone around me constantly wanted to go for a walk or take pictures there for any special occasion.

For whatever reason, I dodged these invitations, and it wasn’t until I was forced to go that I realized what I was missing out on.

In my head, an arboretum is just a collection of trees. I thought to myself, “Why would I want to look at that?” But the arboretum is so much more. There are flowering plants, little instruments, toys and walkways with sitting areas. On a beautiful fall day, it’s the type of place I would want to hang out if I couldn’t be in Beaver Stadium.

Dinner and a movie

If you want to avoid the on-campus crowds and noise of a nighttime Penn State football game, you can always head to downtown State College for dinner and a movie.

Every Penn State student has a favorite downtown restaurant, and pairing a dinner at your restaurant of choice, whether it’s a quick meal at Yallah Taco or a fancy dinner at The Tavern, can really boost the mood. Afterward, the State Theatre is conveniently located nearby for students to see a film or show in a cute, relaxed environment.

Although The State Theatre isn’t always playing the newest movies, you can see what’s playing for the week ahead on its website.

Hike Mount Nittany

You can also go touch grass.

If you don’t have football tickets and need to get away from the happy tailgaters and attendees, take the quick drive off-campus to hike Mount Nittany.

The trailhead in Lemont offers two routes for hikers to take, one of which is about a mile longer than the other, so it’s accessible for hikers of different skill levels. Football season aligns perfectly with fall foliage’s shift to warmer, more orange-hued colors, so the journey promises to be a gorgeous scene.

Go on a trip

Depending on how bitter you are about not being selected for student tickets, you may need to get all the way out of town on gamedays this fall.

If that’s the case, you’re in luck. Penn State isn’t too far from Pittsburgh, Philadelphia, Washington D.C. or New York City. While they may not necessarily be “day trips” — though anything can be a day trip if you wake up early enough — they’re within a reasonable distance for a weekend getaway.

All of these major cities offer a change of pace from University Park, and the museums and entertainment in each one may be a way to get your mind off of the game.

Have a fantastic football-less fall.

title: Staff predictions | How will Penn State fare in its 1st season under Matt Campbell?
author: The Daily Collegian Football Staff
description:
The Matt Campbell era is almost here.

No one is quite sure what Penn State is going to look like in Year 1 under Campbell, but it’s very clear the Nittany Lions have a favorable schedule and a prime opportunity to make some noise with their new head coach.

But will Penn State be able to take advantage of that? Here’s what we think.

Andrew Deal

Regular season record: 10-2

Final result: Loss in quarterfinals of College Football Playoff

Penn State has a difficult four game stretch, playing USC, Michigan and Washington, all teams ranked ahead of the Nittany Lions in the preseason AP Poll. The “big” games may still haunt fans this year, as I see Penn State losing two of those three, both on the road against Michigan and Washington.

Against the Wolverines, Penn State will face the loudest environment of the season, and while Michigan is also led by a first-year head coach in Kyle Whittingham, the environment and defense will prevail in a low-scoring affair.

The Nittany Lions will travel to Washington three weeks later following what should be an easier game against Purdue, and that trip will deal more damage. The Huskies have one of the most versatile quarterbacks in the country in Demond Williams Jr., and his dual threat capabilities mixed with what could be a slow start for Penn State because of West Coast travel will be too much for it to overcome.

Despite under different leadership with James Franklin, Penn State has notoriously started slow against the former Pac-12 squads. In Campbell’s first experience taking his East Coast team to the west, the Nittany Lions won’t quite figure out the best way to travel far and still have a quick start, leading to its second loss of the season.

Outside of those three games, Penn State has a very easy schedule. There’s spots where the team could find difficulties, but I think they can prevail and come out with 10 wins in the regular season. The result will be enough to put the Nittany Lions into the College Football Playoff as the No. 10 seed.

The Nittany Lions outdo expectations in the first round of the College Football Playoff, winning the first round in a hostile environment, with the experience of playing in the Big House earlier helping Rocco Becht and company thrive on the biggest stage.

The run will come to an end in the quarterfinals, falling to one of the top Big Ten teams.

Andrew Mercer

Regular season record: 9-3

Final result: Win bowl game

While Penn State’s schedule to begin the Campbell era is on the weaker side — dodging Ohio State, Oregon and Indiana — growing pains from a slew of transfers and players returning from injury are bound to occur.

Which means an upset could be on the horizon. Specifically, I believe that Northwestern will upset the Nittany Lions, as the Wildcats are playing their first game at the new Ryan Field and want to start the new era on the right foot.

Other than that, the only other potential eyebrow-raiser is Minnesota. Drake Lindsey had a solid redshirt freshman campaign, and Minnesota’s offensive backfield, led by running back Darius Taylor, has a positive outlook. However, the Golden Gophers were winless on the road last season, and that says a lot.

Of the three “difficult” games — Michigan, Washington and USC — I think that Penn State has the best chance at taking down USC in the White Out. The Trojans don’t appear to have a very deep defense, as their backups allowed three consecutive touchdown drives against San Jose State in the fourth quarter, so I think that Penn State will win its signature game.

Michigan and Washington offer distinct challenges because both games are on the road against highly-competitive programs. These games will be close, Washington more than Michigan, but the Nittany Lions will fall regardless.

In a future bowl game, Campbell has the opportunity to show off his younger depth as many of the seniors will likely sit out for the NFL draft. A bowl game victory is a reasonable end to Campbell’s first season while he continues to flesh out the program through recruiting means.

Lexie Linderman

Regular season record: 10-2

Final result: Loss in first round of College Football Playoff

It’s very rare to see a first-year head coach have immediate success at their new program, with Curt Cignetti at Indiana being an outlier. Usually, there’s some growing pains, and I expect Campbell to have a fair share of his own.

But Penn State is too talented and has too easy of a schedule to really stumble in Campbell’s first season. There will be some challenges though, such as road trips to Washington and Michigan, and adjusting to the Big Ten might take some time.

Regardless, the Nittany Lions will hit double digit wins to kick off the Campbell era. They’ll start off strong with three nonconference wins before taking down Wisconsin and Northwestern, giving Penn State a 5-0 record ahead of the White Out against USC.

That will be the first slip up. Penn State will lose to the Trojans in a close contest that will come down to play in the trenches. Former Nittany Lions’ recruiting target Luke Wafle will show exactly why they wanted him with a big game that keeps Penn State’s passing attack at bay.

The next week, however, will be Campbell’s first signature win for the Nittany Lions — a win over Michigan at the Big House. But Penn State’s other tough road game against Washington will result in a loss.

After winning out following the defeat to the Huskies, Penn State’s win over the Wolverines will be enough to get them into the College Football Playoff. As the No. 11 seed, they’ll face No. 6 Indiana, but won’t be able to dethrone the reigning national champions in a close loss.

Noah Aberegg

Regular season record: 11-1

Final result: Loss in first round of College Football Playoff

Matt Campbell’s first season in Happy Valley presents a lot of uncertainty. From roster chemistry to returns from injury for a few stars, many are unsure how Penn State’s season will play out.

The good news for the Nittany Lions is the easier schedule, with their hardest games coming against USC, Michigan and Washington – ranked No. 14, 16 and 17 in the preseason AP Poll. Due to the easier schedule, I believe the Nittany Lions will need one or fewer losses for a chance at a spot in the College Football Playoff.

Penn State will cruise to victory through its first four contests, including one shutout in the nonconference schedule. While they will emerge victorious against Northwestern, the debut of Ryan Field will give Campbell his first true test with Penn State.

The Wildcats will be good practice for the Nittany Lions before USC comes to Happy Valley for the White Out. Becht will lead a game-winning drive against the Trojans to keep Penn State’s undefeated season alive, but the Nittany Lions will ultimately earn their first loss the following week at Michigan.

Campbell’s team will win out the rest of the season, and the Nittany Lions will still earn a spot in the College Football Playoff as one of three Big Ten teams with the Ducks and the Buckeyes.

While Penn State doesn’t face Ohio State during the regular season, the two will face in the first round, with the Buckeyes earning their 10th straight win over the Nittany Lions.

title: 'Fall' in love with these 5 songs perfect for autumn
author: Ally Sons | The Daily Collegian
description:
With the fall season’s official start right around the corner, classes are now in full swing, football season is on its way and there’s plenty of concerts to look forward to.

Starting a new school year can be full of mixed emotions. Whether it's reconnecting with friends, coping with summer ending or a mix of anxiety and excitement about new classes, there’s a lot on the horizon.

If you’re in the market for new songs to both help you navigate those feelings and make it feel like true fall, look no further than these top picks.

1. “oh yeah?” By Steve Lacy

The title song by Steve Lacy on his new album climbed the charts quickly after its release in mid-July.

This song has an indie feel and that “back to campus” vibe students look for. While it’s maybe a little more niche than some of the other picks, this is a good option, especially if you’re looking to broaden your musical horizons.

Slow-paced yet catchy, this is a great addition for your back to school playlist.

2. “End of August” By Noah Kahan

With September’s beginning, this song feels right on the nose. Kahan sings about how it can be scary to acknowledge the changing of the seasons, but reminds listeners that they still have their support systems, and that there are positives to changes, even when they seem scary.

"End of August" covers the sadness of leaving home but also the excitement that comes with a new year and new experiences.

If you’re looking to romanticize your walk to class as the leaves change colors, this is the song for you.

3. “Where You Are” By John Summit

Many students are looking forward to the John Summit concert at the Bryce Jordan Center this October. Having bought their tickets months ago, excitement and anticipation is running high.

In preparation for that concert, this song is a great first look at his music, reminding listeners of the going out scene here at Penn State. There is likely not a single bar or party you could go to without hearing this song at least once.

Whether you’re looking for a new song to play while getting ready with your friends or a song to hype you up for class, this is a popular pick.

4. “Sweater Weather” By The Neighbourhood

When talking about fall songs, you’d be remiss to not put this one on your playlist. “Sweater Weather” is a classic fall song that covers everything from the weather changing to new and old relationships to fall wardrobes.

This song follows the singer describing how the changing weather reminds him of an old relationship. He sings about sharing clothes and feelings and what this time of year means for him.

This is an experience that some college students know all too well, and this song fully describes those emotions.

5. “Sweet Caroline” By Neil Diamond

A true Penn State football student section classic.

Football is a lot of people's favorite part of the fall season, and outside of Zombie Nation’s “Kernkraft 400,” there are very few songs that encompass the feeling of watching the game as much as this one. When it plays, you can almost feel the stadium pulse and see the blue and white shaker poms dance in front of your eyes.

The lyrics describe the importance of focusing on good times and living in the moment, which is a pillar of the Penn State community. Regardless of whether you got football tickets or not, if you listen to this song, it will bring you right back to the stands.

title: Off the record | Oh, the people you’ll meet
author: Miss Behave I The Daily Collegian
description:
Editor’s Note: Off the record is a weekly column written by a fourth-year Collegian staffer under an alias. It aims to promote a space for honest conversations about love, sex and relationships. Those interested in sharing their experiences or submitting a topic can do so through this anonymous form.

As students fill campus for another school year, first dates and budding relationships tend to follow. Is it love in the air, or is it the crippling feeling that yet another situationship is going to fail?

It’s exciting not knowing who you’re going to meet, but it’s intimidating when there are over 80,000 fish in the Penn State sea. While I can’t tell you exactly who you’ll meet, there’s a catalog of characters you’ll find on your journey to romance.

The Shakespearean litterateur

Oftentimes the best writing excludes fluff and redundancy. Every word is carefully picked. Every letter serves a purpose. Achieving such a degree of conciseness comes naturally to many Penn State guys. “Wyd?” is straight to the point and doesn’t beat around the bush. “Can I see you?” falls into this territory as well, demonstrating the repertoire of phrases this character will often use.

You usually can’t learn a lot about a person from a couple of words. On the other hand, when it’s only a couple, it tells you everything you need to know.

A “U up?” text from a frat brother at 11:37 p.m. could be a fun night if that’s what you’re into, but if you’re looking for something more serious, don’t respond. He’s most likely drunk, bored, or probably both. There are no flowers or date nights in the foreseeable future.

The love-bomber

Flowers and chocolate-covered strawberries on the first date make you wonder, “Did this guy come straight out of a rom-com?”

Newsflash, he didn’t. You spend so much time together going for walks, getting dinner downtown and watching both of your favorite movies; it feels romantic and almost too good to be true. If it feels too good to be true, you’ve probably got a love-bomber on your hands.

One random Tuesday you wake up to a, “Hey, I’m just not ready for something right now,” text. It’s laughable, honestly, how ready he seemed 24 hours ago. In my opinion, dealing with this character is probably one of the most painful. You know it can’t be real, but you’re so swept up in the picture-perfect “relationship” until he decides to change his mind.

If a guy is coming on too strong from day one, he was always planning to end it after a week. He wanted to have fun and then quit before there was any chance of commitment.

It’s difficult to not wonder about what you did, but the truth is that you did nothing, and the problem lies with him. A love-bomber can make you feel unwanted, but you have to make sure you don’t internalize these feelings. It’s easier said than done when you have rose-colored glasses on, but the best advice I can give is to not expect anything from the beginning, and find yourself a friend who can give you a reality check.

The figment of your imagination

One minute, you’re having fun together, then the next, he’s gone. He’ll have you questioning reality. Was he real? Did you actually chat and kiss, or was it all just an illusion?

Don’t worry, you’ll probably awkwardly run into him on campus in the future, confirming it wasn’t made up in your head.

Men thrive off of disrespectful communication. Whether it be insulting you to your face or ghosting you, they’ll trick you into thinking they're not like other guys, just to turn out exactly like them.

People are scared of confrontation, so they avoid the situation altogether by acting as if nothing ever happened. It’s not always easy to do so, though, especially for the party being ghosted. The figment of your imagination character is likely to have sex with you and then never speak to you again.

If a guy can’t practice average human decency, you dodged a bullet, even if it hurts like hell. The beauty of a big school like Penn State is that you are likely to meet so many different people with different things to offer.

The dating world can be a struggle, especially when you’re surrounded by men with the emotional intelligence of a small child. But there’s hope — at least I think.

Yours truly,

Miss Behave

title: Borough council approves deal to purchase Addison Court for $15.75 million to prevent redevelopment
author: Jonathon Chiu | The Daily Collegian
description:
The State College Borough Council voted unanimously to approve the agreement to purchase Addison Court from PrimeCore and authorize the borough’s staff to execute the deal.

Addison Court opened in 1994 to offer affordable housing to seniors and people with disabilities in downtown State College. PrimeCore, which took ownership of the building from Beaver Court Associates in May, has plans to demolish it and replace it with a mixed-use structure called Encore.

The borough plans to purchase Addison Court for a total of $15.75 million, according to the deal made with PrimeCore. It’s expected to be fully paid off sometime in 2027, beginning with an initial payment of $250,000 following the council’s vote to approve the deal.

Money from State College’s Inclusionary Housing Fund will also be used to pay for the cost of the purchase, and the borough is expected to continue to work with other partners to acquire additional funds.

The deal also stipulates that the borough will lease Addison Court back to PrimeCore so the company can pursue restoring its status within the Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) tax credit program. Addison Court’s placement within LIHTC expired on Dec. 31, 2024.

The borough is also expected to pay an additional $5 million for the total purchasing costs once the application for LIHTC funding is filed by PrimeCore, according to the terms of the agreement.

If successful, LIHTC funding will likely keep Addison Court affordable for tenants for the next 40 years, and PrimeCore will operate and manage the building during these years as required by the LIHTC program.

State College will be paid an amount between $2 million and $3 million once the application for LIHTC placement is approved.

Should LIHTC funding not be obtained by Feb. 1, 2031, the agreement allows State College to either have PrimeCore repurchase Addison Court, retain ownership of the building or sell the property to a different owner.

Several residents of Addison Court and their supporters, including members of the Centre County Democratic Socialists of America and Central PA United, took their seats at Monday’s borough council meeting to await its decision on whether it would buy the building from PrimeCore Properties.

Centre County Democratic Socialists of America Member Sylus Smith said in a public comment that Addison Court’s residents help to make the borough “truly exceptional” through a more diverse community, which can’t happen if housing unaffordability forces them to move away.

“I can think of no greater responsibility for this council than the preservation of that exception,” Smith, a fourth-year studying political science, said. “It is the unaffordability of housing that tells our senior neighbors, our most vulnerable neighbors at the homes which they have often known for decades, for their entire lives — for longer than I have been alive — that they have to leave.”

Smith concluded his public comment by urging the council to preserve State College as “a place for everyone” by following through with purchasing Addison Court.

Prior to voting on the agreement, several council members praised the actions of community members to help support Addison Court’s tenants in their fight to preserve the building.

“The community came out and made it very clear what their wishes were and council listened, and I want to compliment everyone in our community for doing that,” John Hayes, a council member, said. “In 2026, show me another town, another place or another community that said, ‘Yes, please raise our taxes so we can take care of our most vulnerable citizens,’ and you were very clear that you wanted us to do this and now, tonight, it is going to.”

title: Penn State wrestlers, NLWC bring back 4 gold medals at Poland Open
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
While the collegiate season is still about two months away, Penn State sent representatives to Warsaw, Poland to compete in the 2026 Poland Open.

Across many weight classes, the Nittany Lion connections dominated the field in freestyle, bringing home multiple medals.

Here’s how the wrestlers performed.

Luke Lilledahl, 57 kg, Gold

Luke Lilledahl opened things up with a commanding 10-0 tech fall over Hungary’s Balazs Racz in the first round. Lilledahl earned a spot in the finals with his second tech fall, this time by 11-0 over Switzerland’s Thomas Epp.

Lilledahl took on Puerto Rico’s Darian Cruz, who won the 2017 NCAA Championship at 125 lbs. Lilledahl proved himself on the international stage with a 2-0 win, earning the gold medal over Cruz in Poland.

Marcus Blaze, 61 kg, Gold

Marcus Blaze opened his tournament similarly to Lilledahl, with an 11-0 tech fall over Ukraine’s Yaroslaw Hurskyy. In a tournament that featured many Americans, Blaze took on fellow American Austin DeSanto. In a closer battle, Blaze proved his strong defense once again, defeating DeSanto with a 5-0 victory.

Blaze continued his dominance in the semifinals, taking on another American in Josh Rodriguez. The battle of Nittany Lion Wrestling Club members came out in Blaze’s favor as he won by pinfall over Rodriguez.

Blaze continued and faced his third American of the tournament. In overwhelming fashion, Blaze defeated Kyle Burwick with an 11-0 tech fall, going 4-0 with a gold medal. Blaze finished with three bonus point victories in his four matches, giving him momentum heading into the Senior World Championships.

Josh Rodriguez, 61 kg, 5th place

Josh Rodriguez is a member of the NLWC. His run toward gold ended with a loss to Blaze, but his path to that match included two victories over wrestlers from Georgia. Rodriguez defeated Giorgi Goniashvili by pinfall before narrowly winning a match over Robert Dingashvili, 3-2.

Rodriguez lost a bronze medal match, and ultimately earned fifth place, defaulting to Japan’s Akito Mukaida.

Zain Retherford, 70 kg, Gold

Former Penn State wrestler Zain Retherford was back in action on the international stage at 70 kilograms. Retherford began with an 8-2 victory over American Alec Pantaleo.

Retherford broke out the offense in the next two matches, winning by tech fall and pin against Ukrainian Narek Pohosian and Hungary’s Marton Varga, respectively.

The former Nittany Lion took down Armenia’s Arman Andreasyan by pin, capping off a truly dominant day. Retherford finished with a 4-0 record, earning three bonus victories to end his tournament.

Levi Haines, 79 kg, Gold

While all the talk surrounding Levi Haines has been about him possibly having a fifth year — which he no longer has the opportunity to use — Haines continues to dominate in freestyle.

Haines pinned Poland’s Fabian Niedźiedzki in his home country to begin his day. Haines met a familiar foe in his next match, defeating former Iowa wrestler Patrick Kennedy by tech fall, 12-2, continuing his path to gold.

Haines took down Germany’s David Wolf Stas by tech fall in the next round, heading to the gold medal match. Haines faced off against Georgia’s Luka Chkhitunidze and won by pinfall again to stand atop the podium. Haines continues to build up for a Senior World Championship run at the end of October.

Cole Mirasola, 125 kg, 5th

Cole Mirasola continues to compete in the heavyweight class as he tries to acclimate to the weight class despite still being undersized. His size played a factor in a fifth-place finish in Poland.

Mirasola began with a 12-1 tech fall over American Jacob Bullock, proving his technique is still near the top amongst his opponents.

Mirasola dropped his next match against Germany’s Mohsen Mansour Siyar by a score of 13-7. The Nittany Lion defeated fellow American Crew Howard, 7-3, before dropping his bronze medal match by an 11-0 tech fall against American Jordan Wood.

Mirasola finished his Poland Open with a 2-2 record at 125 kilograms.

Most of Penn State’s wrestlers who competed in the Poland Open will continue to wrestle freestyle up until the start of the collegiate folkstyle season.
