title: Women's soccer coach Erica Dambach earns 300th Penn State win, thumps Bucknell
author: Gavin Leonard | The Daily Collegian
description:
The Nittany Lions hosted the Bucknell Bison at Jeffrey Field at 7:30 pm on Thursday. Penn State bounced back after a 1-2 loss against West Virginia.

Coach Erica Dambach earned her 300th win in her career with the Nittany Lions after a dominant 5-0 win against the Bison.

“Overall, one of my top five nights of my career,” Dambach said. “I couldn’t even keep my emotions together, and then walking off of (the field), I think I'm even more emotional than I was before the game started, and that's saying a lot.”

Bucknell kicked off the match with possession of the ball in the Nittany Lions half, yet the white and blue defended their first offensive push well.

For the first five minutes of the game, both squads battled defensively, not allowing the opposing offenses to hold possession for long stints.

Penn State's first set piece of the match was a corner kick that was batted down by Bucknell’s goalkeeper, which she then collected.

A notable defensive stop came from defender Kayleigh Herr. A clearance attempt bounced off a Penn State defender and landed in the possession of a Bucknell attacker. Herr made a sliding tackle to stop a potential goal.

Penn State's attackers kept sending passes to teammates making runs, but the Bison defenders shielded them well.

Another mishandled goal kick by Penn State's defense almost led to a goal when Bucknell’s attack took several shots at the goal that were blocked near the goalline by both Mackenzie Gress and two defenders.

While their inability to track goalkicks was an early concern for the Nittany Lions, they were able to hold possession, leading to early corner kicks and shot attempts. When the defense didn’t make self-inflicted mistakes, the team controlled the match.

That control of the ball paid off when Paige Pasinski scored the opening goal of the game, slotting the ball into the bottom left corner of the goal after an assist from Aubrey Kulpa to take a 1-0 lead. The Nittany Lions methodically moved downfield by playing from the back, making runs, and finding the open man.

Bucknell’s defense played a low-line, waiting to pressurize the ball around midfield, but the white and blue handled the disruption well. Nittany Lion defenders passed back and forth until finding a midfielder making a run or sitting in space waiting to receive the ball.

Yet, the Bisons’ defense bent but didn’t break, defending various corner kicks and offensive pushes made by the Nittany Lions.

At around nine minutes left in the half, the white and blue defense played a bit sloppily in its defensive third. A poor clearance attempt led to a corner kick opportunity, in which a header sailed wide of the goal.

After the ball was cleared, Ellie Kocher received it around midfield, made a nice run down the left side, outpacing a defender in the process, before her shot went wide right.

With three minutes left, the Nittany Lions had all the momentum. A shot on goal outside the box led to a corner kick for the white and blue. Paige Kalal sent the kick back post for Lily Burger, who headed the ball into the back of the net to head into halftime with a 2-0 lead.

Even with the lead, the Nittany Lions didn’t play a perfect brand of soccer.

“I thought the game was played on their terms in the second half,” Dambach said. It’s hard when teams are putting balls on top of you to then settle the game.”

Coach Dambach’s message at halftime was to return to their style of play, and that’s exactly what they did.

To begin the half, Bucknell played with more defenders back to stop Penn State from making runs in the middle of the field.

That didn’t stop the Nittany Lions from finding ways to get open, when a through ball was sent into the box and chased down by Kocher. The Bucknell goalie attempted to slide tackle Kocher, but clipped her legs instead, resulting in a penalty kick for the white and blue. Bucknell challenged the call but was unsuccessful.

Hannah Jordan’s penalty was saved, but the goalkeeper's failure to catch the ball resulted in a rebound back to Jordan and a goal to take a 3-0 lead in the first couple minutes of the second half.

Penn State began to dominate on both ends of the field. The Nittany Lion attack was firing on all cylinders with multiple shots on goal within a five-minute span, while the defense limited passes on their side of the field.

That trend continued with a goal from Aubrey Kulpa that hit the right post and bounced in for Kulpa’s second goal contribution of the night. A pass was sent in by Anna Babcock for her first career assist.

With 21 minutes left in the match, the white and blue kept making the game look easy. Another goal was scored by Kaelyn Wolfe on the right side of the box, which was assisted by Nicole Crane. The Nittany Lions took a commanding 5-0 lead.

The Nittany Lions can thank their defense for a portion of their second-half offensive success, as they’ve put an end to every attack that Bucknell has attempted to put together. The defense finished the game with something to show for it, as they earned their first clean sheet of the season.

“They held it down back there,” Aubrey Kulpa said. “They do their job, and they encourage us. They build out of the back and then we can do our job.”

Up Next

The Nittany Lions will host Brown on Sunday at 1:30 pm for the Alumni Day and Senior Day match. Before the game will be the March to the Match promotion, as fans can enjoy the Happy Valley tradition.

title: Penn State LB Tony Rojas on Hispanic College Football Player of the Year Award watch list
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Another preseason recognition for a Nittany Lion.

Penn State linebacker Tony Rojas was named to the Hispanic College Football Player of the Year Award watch list on Thursday, given to the nation's top Hispanic player.

Rojas is coming off a season-ending injury last season, but will be back to play for Week 1 against Marshall.

Prior to his injury, Rojas was on pace for a career year, totaling 25 tackles in just four games. He was instrumental to the Nittany Lions' defensive success in 2024, where he totaled 58 tackles and three interceptions en route to a College Football Playoff semifinal appearance.

Rojas will be one of the starting linebackers for Penn State in 2026, leading a very veteran-heavy linebacker room.

The redshirt junior has also been named to the Comeback Player of the Year Award watch list and the Lott IMPACT Trophy watch list ahead of the 2026 season.

title: Penn State notebook | Rob Dow talks men's soccer matchup against Pittsburgh
author: Ava Aguiar | The Daily Collegian
description:
After an intense loss against Missouri State saw both sophomore defender Joe Buckley and coach Rob Dow ejected and sidelined for their upcoming match, the Nittany Lions will look to regain their confidence as they take on Pittsburgh in another nonconference matchup.

Both teams currently sit at 1-1, with the Panthers coming off a 3-1 win against Bucknell. With strong midfielders like Grayson Carter, Logan Oliver and ex-Nittany Lion Caden Grabfelder, Penn State will have to focus its efforts on keeping the ball and going against the Panthers' strong counterpress.

“Defensively, we must stay compact, not get stretched out,” Dow said. “They’re typically pretty good in possessing and balancing teams on the ball, but we’re excited.”

As the team tries to rebuild after finishing last in the Big Ten two years ago and losing all but three players from their previous season, coach Dow will rely on key returnee Amadou Kone.

“He’s a direct, fast, tenacious attacking player that can convert and create for sure,” Dow said. “But once he gets into space, that’s when he comes alive.”

Kone, who assisted the blue and white’s first and only goal against the Bears, will has an opportunity to continue his play, leaving enough space behind the wide back for him to attack the ball and get in a groove.

Dow will also have the likes of Nehan Hassan, one of the newest faces for the blue and white.

“He’s playing above his years; he’s a young player, but he doesn’t feel like a young player in the program,” Dow said. “When he picks up the ball, things happen. He can eliminate the first player, the second player, a top-tier player.”

Penn State also looks to play to their strengths during the match to compete against the Panthers' offensive plays, prioritizing the set piece.

“I think we’ll have the quality of advantage against Pitt on corners, on direct free kicks, Joe Sheridan’s vicious height, Toby Grant’s vertical jump, the onset of Bill Forester,” Dow said. “We're getting good service to those guys so that’ll be a big focus.”

With Dow being out, Brad Cole will fill in as interim coach during the match. A standout player himself in college, Cole has knowledge on and off the field, having worked under Dow in his previous role at Vermont.

“We have a tremendous amount of trust and respect for each other,” Dow said. “But he’ll do an amazing job in the program, probably better.”

title: Jerry Sandusky to return to court for evidentiary hearing
author: Kahlie Wray | Editor-in-Chief
description:
Jerry Sandusky will return to the Centre County Courthouse on Sept. 8 at 9:30 a.m. for an evidentiary hearing, according to a court order.

The former Penn State assistant football coach was convicted in 2012 of sexually abusing young boys. He was originally sentenced to 30 to 60 years in prison.

The order does not specify what will be addressed at the hearing. Sandusky has been challenging his sexual abuse conviction for years.

Senior Judge Maureen A. Skerda will be presiding over the case.

title: 5 Penn State field hockey players named to NFHCA Collegiate Watch List
author: Noah Radio | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State field hockey players Josephine Purdy, Ella Gaitan, Natalie Freeman, Sienna Dunn and Abygail Deverka were named to the National Field Hockey Coaches Association watch list on Thursday.

Purdy, a sophomore midfielder/forward from Virginia Beach, Virginia, is looking to take a leap after a strong first season. She scored six goals in 2025 in 17 games and started two.

Gaitan is a third-year forward who transferred to Penn State from Maryland earlier this year. With the Terrapins, the Belvidere, New Jersey, native appeared in 34 games and started 31.

Freeman returns to the Nittany Lions for her senior season after starting all 17 games last year and contributing seven points. The midfielder/forward has appeared in every game in the last three seasons.

Dunn, a graduate student from Peel, Isle of Man, England, will make her debut in the blue and white on Friday. She was a member of England’s U21, U18 and U16 teams and served as captain of the England U21 team at the 2025 Junior World Cup.

Deverka, a Houston, Texas native, has started 29 games in goal for Penn State. In 2025, she racked up 70 saves and allowed 40 goals. The junior has a .648 career save percentage and 138 career saves.

The Nittany Lions are set to face No. 5 Virginia at 4:00 pm on Friday.

title: SEE IT: Penn State women's volleyball announces T-shirt giveaway for regular season opener
author: Elliott Inscho | Sports Editor
description:
Penn Staters attending the opening match of the blue and white’s 2026 campaign will be adding to their wardrobe.

The Nittany Lions have announced that the first 500 students at Saturday’s match against UConn will receive a free “Serve Notice” T-shirt.

First serve is set for 4 p.m. at Rec Hall, with doors opening an hour prior.

title: Penn State men’s soccer presented with chance to bounce back against Pittsburgh
author: Luci Palacios | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State will look to bounce back from its first loss of the season when it hosts Pittsburgh at 7 p.m. Friday at Jeffrey Field.

The Nittany Lions enter the matchup 1-1 after opening the season with a 3-2 win over Mercyhurst before falling 3-1 to Missouri State on the road. Pittsburgh also holds a 1-1 record after losing 2-1 to then-No. 7 Maryland in its opener before responding with a 3-1 win over Bucknell.

Notably, a familiar face will return to Happy Valley in Friday’s matchup, this time representing the opposing team.

On July 28, former Nittany Lion star midfielder Caden Grabfelder transferred to Pittsburgh after three seasons with Penn State. Grabfelder appeared in 49 games during his time at Happy Valley, recording nine goals and nine assists before joining the Panthers.

Grabfelder was one of Penn State’s main contributors last season, starting 14 of 16 games and finishing with two goals and five assists. His move to Pittsburgh gives the Nittany Lions an early contest against a player who already knows the team and its home field well.

The Panthers are coming off a rough 6-7-5 season in 2025, while Penn State finished 5-8-4. Both teams have a chance to put those records behind them after getting their first wins of the new season.

Just as Pittsburgh rebounded with a two-goal win over Bucknell, Penn State looks for a similar response after its loss to Missouri State. The Nittany Lions took an early lead when senior midfielder Luca Sowinski scored his first collegiate goal in the 18th minute, with senior forward Amadou Kone earning his first collegiate assist on the play.

Missouri State tied the game before halftime and took control early in the second half, scoring just one minute after the break. The Bears added another goal from the penalty box in the 51st minute before things took a turn for the worse for the Nittany Lions.

Freshman Joe Buckley was sent off in the 56th minute after receiving his second yellow card of the match. Coach Rob Dow was also ejected later in the game after receiving a red card, meaning both he and Buckley will be unavailable against Pittsburgh.

The Nittany Lions will have to adjust without their coach and one of their defenders, but also have a chance to use Friday’s game as a reset. Penn State has historically controlled the series, holding a 24-9-4 record across 36 meetings with the Panthers.

However, Pittsburgh has had the upper hand in recent years, going 3-2-2 against the Nittany Lions since 2008. The Panthers won the most recent meeting, a 2-1 victory at Jeffrey Field in 2024.

With both teams sitting at 1-1, Friday’s matchup gives Penn State a chance to move back above .500 while facing a former teammate and a Pittsburgh team looking to build off its first win of the season.

title: Position preview | Penn State’s LBs bring depth to defense
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State’s linebacker room has a much different look entering this season.

After bringing in four players from Iowa State, retaining Tony Rojas and adding several younger players, linebacker is one of the deepest positions on the Nittany Lions’ roster this year, a stark contrast from last season when depth was thin.

Here’s a look at Penn State’s linebackers ahead of the 2026 season.

Starters

After his redshirt sophomore season was cut short due to a torn ACL, Tony Rojas announced his return for a fourth year to Happy Valley. He’s been a consistent starter the last two years and made a major impact on the field during his healthy sophomore season.

Rojas’ breakout season came in 2024 when he recorded 58 tackles, six tackles for loss and a trio of interceptions — including a pick six against SMU in the first round of the College Football Playoff. He’s had to adapt to new defensive coordinator D’Anton Lynn’s scheme while rehabbing.

“I feel great,” Rojas said at local media day on Aug. 7. “Feels good to be back and can’t wait for the season.”

Taking the MIKE role and wearing the green dot is Kooper Ebel, who came over from Iowa State with Matt Campbell.

Ebel has also been a full-time starter the last two seasons, but has been more effective in run defense than Rojas. He’s recorded 149 tackles, 14 tackles for loss and a pair of sacks over the past three years.

The third starter entering this season will be another one of Campbell’s former products. Cael Brezina slowly made a name for himself through two seasons at Iowa State, but has had even more success this offseason.

When discussing Brezina’s work during fall camp, Campbell said his performance has been “the best football he’s seen Cael Brezina play, maybe in his career.”

Role players

Caleb Bacon started all 12 games for Iowa State last season, with many thinking he’d see a similar role with the Nittany Lions.

However, Campbell discussed during local media day a potential move to defensive end for the Iowa State transfer, as Bacon said “I think I'm really just ready for whatever.”

Bacon will likely split time between both positions after a standout redshirt junior year with the Cyclones, where he recorded 68 tackles, 9.5 tackles for loss and three sacks.

Sophomore Alex Tatsch — one of the few returners to Penn State’s linebacker room — played in six games and recorded 14 tackles during his true freshman campaign.

Tatsch picked up an injury before the Pinstripe Bowl that left him sidelined much of the offseason. However, Campbell said on Aug. 13 that he’s trending positively through recovery, but didn’t indicate whether he’d be available for Week 1.

Depth pieces

The Nittany Lions have many young players with little to no collegiate playing experience who could provide depth to this year’s linebacker room if needed.

Redshirt freshman Cam Smith is the most talked about of those remaining six linebackers on Penn State’s squad, as Campbell said on Aug. 25 that he’s “gotten better every day.”

John Klosterman is one of the more veteran linebackers on the team after four seasons at Iowa State, but he’s only played in 24 games and recorded 18 tackles during his career.

Sophomore Chris Fileppo comes from West Virginia, where he made one start and an additional 11 appearances as a true freshman.

The Nittany Lions have three additional freshmen linebackers in Keian Kaiser, Josh Banks and Evan Wolff who may see the field as a result of redshirt seasons ultimately being eliminated.

title: Penn State field hockey opens season hosting Virginia, Lock Haven
author: Rafael Rivera | The Daily Collegian
description:
The Hannah Prince era in Happy Valley is looming with Penn State’s season right around the corner. The team will start the season in State College, playing a pair of Games against Virginia on Thursday and Lock Haven on Sunday.

Prince comes into the Nittany Lions head coaching job with top-notch experience at the collegiate Level. As coach of St Joseph's, she led the team to a historic National Championship appearance in 2024 and also registered a 64-24 record across her four seasons with the Red Hawks, collecting NCAA tournament appearances in each of those years. In her last season, she guided St Joseph’s to its fifth straight Atlantic 10 championship title. Prince has an opportunity to bring this experience to a Penn State team that struggled during the 2025 season.

The Nittany Lions are led by senior midfielder Natalie Freeman. The Ellicott City, Maryland, native, is expected to be Penn State’s primary goal scorer in 2026 after a stellar 2025 season in which she notched 19 points in 17 matches. Over her career, Freeman logged a total of 26 points in 32 games.

Virginia

In 31 all-time meetings against the Cavaliers, Penn State leads the series 21-11, but the Cavaliers have won the last two matchups, with the most recent meeting resulting in a 5-1 Virginia win in 2025. Last season was a good one for the Cavaliers, going 16-3, losing in the ACC Championship.

Senior breakout Mia Abello is Virginia’s best attacking threat, putting up 20 points in 19 games played en route to All ACC-First Team honors in 2025. Last year, Abello had one assist against Penn State and enters again as a threat for the blue and white defense.

The Cavaliers enter Happy Valley as one of the nation's top contenders, with the No. 5 spot in the preseason NFHCA Poll, as it poses an immediate test for Prince’s squad to jump right into the fire.

Virginia is also an extremely different squad from last season, with seven true freshmen, four of whom were ranked inside the nation's top-50 in the class, proving the Cavaliers carry a scary mix of both youth and veteran talent.

Lock Haven

To round out the weekend, Lock Haven comes to State College to take on the Nittany Lions in a 46th all-time matchup where the blue and white leads the series 20-22-3.

The last time these two teams matched up in 2025, Penn State won in an 8-0 thrashing where Freeman and Ella Jennes led the charge with the pair combining for five goals.

Lock Haven had a season to forget in 2025, going 2-16. With such a disappointing result on the pitch, the Bald Eagles appointed Valerie Clarke as the new head coach in May. The new boss arrives at Lock Haven after a successful tenure with Converse University, where Clarke had coached since 2018.

At Converse, Clarke earned numerous accolades, including back-to-back South Atlantic Conference Tournament Championships in 2021 and 2022, which helped her earn SAC Coach of the Year honors.

The new appointments go head-to-head directly in their second games with their new squads, with Clarke making her away debut with Lock Haven.

title: Penn State’s women’s volleyball follows Spikes Under the Lights with Penn State Invitational
author: Ashley Felsberg I The Daily Collegian
description:
After its appearance in Spikes Under the Lights, Penn State women’s volleyball is kicking off its nonconference play in the Penn State Invitational on Saturday. The Nittany Lions will play three matches throughout the weekend, against UConn, Hofstra and High Point.

Coach Katie Schumacher-Cawley's squad closed its last season in round two of the NCAA Tournament, after being swept by the Texas Longhorns — a bit of a letdown, as the blue and white were the previous reigning champions after its triumphant run in 2024, going 35-2.

Penn State has a powerful duo at its forefront this year. Florida transfers Alexis Stucky and Kennedy Martin form a powerful setter and right-side tag team. Stucky is beginning her first season with the Nittany Lions this year, but Martin transferred to Penn State prior to the 2025 season.

On Saturday, the Nittany Lions will face off against the UConn Huskies. The two teams have only seen each other nine times and only once this millennium, when Penn State won in a sweep in 2022.

UConn has reinforcements all over the court, with a large veteran presence in the front row and a stable libero in the back.

Senior Grace Maria has been at UConn since her freshman year. As a first-year, she appeared in 26 matches. After that, she constantly appeared in every game of her sophomore and junior seasons and is expected to lead in the front again this year.

She was named to the Bearcat Classic All-Tournament Team and totaled 146 kills, 36 aces, 71 blocks and 170 digs on the season.

Along with Maria, senior Isabella Suhy adds reinforcement to the Husky back line. As libero, Suhy totaled 85 digs last year, and 245 digs in her UConn career thus far. Just last season in the Huskies' match against Seton Hall, she reached a season high of 16 digs.

On Sunday, Penn State will play two matches: one at 10 a.m. and one at 6 p.m. The blue and white will first face off against High Point.

High Point and Penn State have never met in program history.

The Panthers haven’t altered a majority of its roster. They are holding onto 10 players and adding five new freshmen and one Virginia Tech transfer. Since around 90% of the roster played together last season, their chemistry is at the core of their offense.

Penn State will conclude its three-match weekend at 6 p.m. Sunday against the Hofstra Pride. In program history, the two teams have met nine times, but not in recent years. Their latest match was in 2019, where Penn State won 3-0.

The Pride are led by CAA honorees Beatriz Braga and Constanza Perez Sain. Braga was named CAA Preseason Player of the Year on August 19th and both players were named to the Preseason All-CAA Team.

While each team poses its own defensive threats, offensive duos and veteran experience, Penn State is favored in each match. They are currently ranked No. 10 in the NCAA’s AVCA rankings, whereas the other three are not in the Top 25.

title: A glance at Penn State women’s volleyball’s transfer, recruiting newcomers for the 2026 season
author: Lily Dorf | The Daily Collegian
description:
As the 2026 Women’s Volleyball season begins on Thursday, new faces will be taking the court as Nittany Lions. The team welcomed seven new athletes this year, including four freshman recruits and three transfers.

Here’s a brief overview of each player.

Freshman Recruits

Kendall Northern

Kendall Northern is a 6-foot-1 middle blocker from Cincinnati, who was ranked nationally as Prep Dig’s No. 13 high school recruit in the class of 2026.

In her senior year, she won Gatorade 2025-2026 Player of the Year with 601 kills and 273 digs. She played on Summit Country Day High School’s varsity team all four years, racking up 1,236 kills and 538 digs by the end of her high school career.

Danielle Whitmire

Another recruit stepping onto the court is 6-foot-2 setter Whitmire from Celina, Texas.

She arrives in Happy Valley as Penn State’s highest-rated freshman via Dig Prep, standing at No. 4 nationally. Whitmire played for Walnut Grove High School as well as Texas Advantage Volleyball Club.

Whitmire was on Walnut Grove’s varsity team all four years, racking up 1,100 kills and an 89.9 percent serving percentage. Most notably, she played for USAVolleyball’s 2025 girls U19 (Under 19) national team.

Haley Burgdorf

Joining Northern and Whitmire this season is 6-foot outside hitter Burgdorf, hailing from St. Charles, Illinois.

Burgdorf is ranked No. 29 nationally for the 2026 season via Prep Dig. During her high school career, Burgdorf racked up a combined 695 kills and 309 digs during her freshman and senior years on varsity. She was named Illinois’ Gatorade’s 2025-2026 Player of the Year and Under Armor’s All-American Volleyball Team in 2025.

Finley Krystkowiak

The final commit for the Penn State Nittany Lions is 6-foot-4 outside hitter Krystkowiak.

She was Prep Dig’s No. 10 recruit and hails from San Diego, California. Krystkowiak previously played for Torrey Pines High School and Wave Volleyball Club. During her high school career, Krystkowiak racked up 1,344 kills and 922 digs during her four years on varsity.

Krystkowiak comes from an all-star family, with twin sister Samantha Krystkowiak playing beach volleyball for Stanford University, and father Larry Krystkowiak playing in the NBA, most notably with the Chicago Bulls.

The newcomers will make their debut at Spikes Under the Light in Arlington, Texas on Aug. 27.

Transfers

Alexis Stucky

Along with the incoming recruits, 6-foot-2 setter Stucky will be joining the Nittany Lions. Stucky is a redshirt senior from Laramie, Wyoming, and transferred in from Florida.

Stucky and star teammate Kennedy Martin both previously played for the Gators and are reunited once again as teammates. Stucky played four seasons with Florida, where she totaled 626 digs, 80 aces, 3,047 assists and 167 total blocks.

Ryla Jones

The next transfer is 6-foot-2 middle blocker Jones. She’s a junior from Oxon Hill, Maryland, who transferred from Pittsburgh.

Jones played two seasons as a Panther, totaling 230 kills, 212 total blocks and 22 assists across 62 matches. During her debut year, Jones was named to the All-ACC Freshman Team.

Whitney Lauenstein

The last transfer of the season is 6-foot-2 outside hitter Lauenstein from Waverly, Nebraska. Lauenstein is a graduate student who transferred from Texas, totaling 36 kills, 89 total attacks, 15 total blocks and 12 digs across her previous two seasons.

Lauenstein also played for Nebraska her freshman and sophomore years, totaling 359 kills, 953 total attacks, 123 digs and 136 total blocks.

title: Former Penn State RB Miles Sanders arrested for driving under the influence
author: Lexie Linderman | Football Editor
description:
Former Penn State running back Miles Sanders was arrested June 8 in Churchill Borough near Pittsburgh for driving under the influence, according to court documents.

Sanders was charged with driving under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance and careless driving. His preliminary hearing is set for Oct. 28.

Sanders played for the Nittany Lions from 2016-18, where he became the 45th player in Penn State history to rush for over 1,000 yards and was a second-team All-Big Ten selection in 2018.

The Pittsburgh native was drafted in the second round of the 2018 NFL Draft to the in-state Philadelphia Eagles. Sanders spent four years with the Eagles before spending 2023-24 with the Carolina Panthers.

Sanders most recently played for the Dallas Cowboys in 2025, but only appeared in four games due to injury. He is currently a free agent.

title: Penn State DT Siale Taupaki taking initiative, guiding defensive line
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
In order to hold up against a Big Ten offense, Penn State’s defensive line must be the best it can possibly be. Defensive tackle Siale Taupaki knows this all too well after spending the past seven seasons at UCLA before becoming a Nittany Lion.

Having that experience under his belt has given him enough wisdom to act as the defensive line’s mentor and role model. Taupaki has taken it upon himself to guide both his fellow veterans and the younger generation to get the whole unit on the same page.

Taupaki has been setting up one-on-one meetings as a way of keeping people accountable and to leave no doubt in anyone’s mind about what to do and how to do it. It’s also a way to keep himself in the mix because regardless of his age, he’s still in a position to learn from anyone on the roster.

“I believe that one-on-one meetings with each of the players is beneficial because you get to actually pick and see where they're coming from, how they dissect the information that they see on the field,” Taupaki said on Tuesday. “After we're done with the field, we come back together and I say ‘Shoot it to me, what do you see? How can I help? How do you play the game?’”

While Taupaki has an instinctive urge to lead, he doesn’t credit that as a desire to coach in the future. For him, it’s just baked into his nature. He said that from a young age, he’s always taken initiative in these situations purely of his own accord.

It’s also a culmination of his observations from “being around great people” and watching those individuals play football in their own ways and with their own unique styles.

“Everybody learns in a different way,” Taupaki said. “Some guys are better at being in the meeting room versus some guys who are better on the field, going through it, walk-through, seeing it for themselves. So I try to learn everyone because that's who I am too.”

Despite not being interested in coaching at this time, Taupaki’s words about how great of a teacher D’Anton Lynn is closely echoed the description that he gave himself.

“With Lynn, there's certain things that he wants done, but then his doors are always open for us to come up to find the little knicks and knacks that we can fix,” Taupaki said. “That's one thing that I truly like because if you’ve ever been with someone that they like stuff a certain way, you try to go in and talk to them, but they don't want to. It's different with Lynn.”

Ahead of his first and only season at Penn State, Taupaki’s message was clear. Each individual defensive player has to be completely ready at all times.

“Between now and gameday, I believe that what I need to succeed personally is understanding, going towards that game, that each of my guys are gonna do their job,” Taupaki said. “If you stay prepared, you'll be ready. But until then, I want to make sure that the guys and I are all on the same page fundamentally, technically, communicating. I want to be able to have that mindset. Other than that, let's just play ball.”

Penn State's quest for another conference title won't be far from State College.

title: No. 10 Penn State women’s volleyball set to open season in Spikes Under the Lights tournament in Dallas
author: Elliott Inscho | Sports Editor
description:
Penn State’s 2026 campaign starts on one of the biggest stages that collegiate women’s volleyball has ever been played on.

The Nittany Lions are heading to Arlington, Texas, where they’ll participate in the Spikes Under the Lights tournament at AT&T Stadium, the home of the Dallas Cowboys.

Katie Schumacher-Cawley’s squad will have a chance to set the tone for the year after being eliminated by No. 3 Texas in the NCAA second round to close last season. Here’s everything you need to know for the historic event in the Lone Star State.

The format

Spikes Under the Lights will see four preeminent women’s volleyball teams take to the court on national television, although the matches will officially go down as best-of-three-set exhibitions.

The first serve of the night will come in the bracket’s opening match, being played between Nebraska and Florida at 8:00 p.m. Then, the Nittany Lions will take to the court at 9:00 p.m. for their season debut against SMU.

After those matches conclude, the winners will meet for the tournament championship at 10:00 p.m.

The participants

Penn State will be thrown directly into the fire to begin the season, as all of the squads in the four-team tournament were ranked in the AVCA preseason poll.

SMU placed No. 11 to start the year, one spot below the blue and white. Spikes Under the Lights won’t be the first on-court action of the year for the Mustangs, though.

They opened their season on Sunday with a sweep of No. 8 Texas A&M as part of the AVCA First Serve tournament. Sophomore outside hitter Suli Davis led SMU with 15 kills in her first match as a Mustang after transferring from BYU.

On the other side of the bracket, Florida will provide a familiar challenge for Kennedy Martin and Alexis Stucky, who both began their career in Gainesville.

The Gators slotted in at No. 17 in the AVCA’s opening poll after posting a 16-12 record last season. Their season ended in the NCAA second round when they were swept by SMU, but Florida could potentially set up a rematch in the tournament championship if they can take down Nebraska.

It won’t be easy, though. Nebraska was ranked No. 1 overall to open the year, and received 57 out of 63 total first-place votes.

The Cornhuskers are led by middle blocker Andi Jackson, outside hitter Harper Murray and setter Bergen Reilly, who each earned unanimous All-Big Ten preseason honors.

The only other unanimous addition to that list? Kennedy Martin.

What’s at stake

A total of $1 million is to be awarded on Thursday night.

Each program will receive $200,000 for participating in the tournament, with an additional $200,000 going to the team that ultimately claims the championship. It’s the largest prize pool ever up for grabs in the history of women’s college sports.

Even though the matches won’t go on the teams’ official record, the high-level matchups will provide a strong opportunity to build momentum early in the season.

For the Nittany Lions, they’ll look to seize on that chance after losing 13 matches last season, the most in a single campaign for the blue and white since they lost 15 in 1982.

The “three-hour primetime event” will be broadcast on TBS starting at 8:00 p.m.

title: Penn State's James Peoples, Chase Sowell named to Earl Campbell Tyler Rose Award watch list
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Another day, another set of Nittany Lions with preseason recognition.

Penn State running back James Peoples and wide receiver Chase Sowell were named to the Earl Campbell Tyler Rose Award watch list, awarding the nation's top offensive player both on and off the field.

Peoples will begin his first year at Penn State after transferring from Ohio State. He rushed for 541 yards and five touchdowns in two seasons with the Buckeyes, but is in contention for the top running back spot with the Nittany Lions.

Sowell made his way from Iowa State and is expected to be one of Rocco Becht's go-to options at receiver. Sowell totaled 500 yards receiving on 32 catches in his lone year with the Cyclones.

With both players expected to make a major impact on and off the field for the Nittany Lions in 2026, the duo is primed to be in contention for the Earl Campbell Tyler Rose Award at the end of the season.

title: Penn State Athletics announces purchasable fan experiences
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
In the new era of NIL and revenue sharing, Penn State has announced another way to increase funding.

Penn State Athletics announced purchasable fan experiences, which will "bring fans of the Nittany Lions closer to the action."

Among the experiences fans can purchase are postgame press conference access, spending a quarter with announcers Steve Jones and Jack Ham, a tailgate visit from the Nittany Lion and more.

Fans can pay $2,063 for a four-person group to experience Matt Campbell's postgame press conference. The same price applies for a two-person group to be in the press box with Jones and Ham for a quarter.

If fans want to be involved with Penn State's spirit squad, there's three different options. They can pay $698 for a visit from the Nittany Lion and cheerleaders to their tailgate lot, pay $2,578 to conduct a song for the Penn State Blue Band with one guest or pay $1,033 to spend time with the Lionettes before kickoff in a two-person group.

Athletics also offers options for fans to take part in pregame setup, with a $1,033 bundle for four people to help set up Beaver Stadium or $3,608 for two people to help set up the locker room.

The final offer is a locker room pregame walkthrough, which a group of four can pay $5,133 to experience before the game.

title: Penn State women's soccer hosts Bucknell and Brown
author: Sara Castrovinci | The Daily Collegian
description:
After drawing against then-No. 2 Notre Dame and falling to then-No. 22 West Virginia, Penn State is back on its home turf this week with a chance to make its first addition to the win column.

The Nittany Lions open their season’s home play against Bucknell at 7:30 p.m. on Aug. 27 and Brown at 1 p.m. on Aug. 30.

The blue and white’s roster experienced big changes from the previous season with a now younger team this year, but the lineup is far from incapable of taking on a competitive season of play.

Looking at the Thursday and Sunday matchups, here’s what to expect.

Thursday vs. Bucknell

Bucknell and Penn State haven’t met since the 2016 season, when the blue and white easily defeated the Bison 6-0 in the NCAA Tournament at Jeffrey Field. The all-time series white stands at 19-0-1 in Penn State's favor, dating back to the early 2000s.

The Bison have been off to a hot start this season, coming into the week with a 3-1 record. Over the four games, Bucknell tallied 13 goals, including eight against Mount St. Mary’s and four against La Salle.

Freshman midfielder Ingrid Murphy is the Bison’s leading goal scorer, accounting for three of their 13 goals. Additionally, Murphy has seven shots on goal and one assist, proving to be an attacking force for Bucknell and emphasizing their offensive-heavy start to the season.

Penn State has managed 20 shots in two games while the Bison has had 83 in four.

Unlike Penn State, Bucknell has yet to play any ranked opponents. Despite this, the Bison still bring an attacking force to the Thursday night matchup under the lights at Jeffrey Field.

Sunday vs Brown

The Sunday afternoon match is the first time the two programs have met on the pitch since 2008, when Brown clinched a 1-0 overtime win against Penn State.

Both Brown and Penn State will come into the matchup with three games under their sleeves after the Bears play UConn and the Nittany Lions face Bucknell Thursday night. Brown is currently 1-1 with a 4-0 win against New Haven and a 1-0 loss against Holy Cross.

The Bears have been a dominant team in the Ivy League with 16 overall conference championships and being picked third in the Ivy League’s preseason poll.

Brown returns Joy Okonye, the 2025 Ivy League Offensive Player of the Year as well as a First Team All-Ivy pick. In the 2025 season, Okonye tallied 19 points with seven goals and five assists, deeming a potential threat this Sunday.

Over the last six seasons, the Bears finished first in the Ivy League regular season four times, showcasing their ability to dominate their conference. Brown will get the chance to showcase its skills this Sunday in the nearly two-decade-awaited rematch since the 2008 UConn Classic.

What to watch for Penn State

The Nittany Lions are still searching for their first regular season win and are hoping to do so in front of their fans.

With the transition into the new season, the blue and white suffered huge losses of Amelia White, Olivia Borgen, Kaitlyn MacBean and Julia Raich. MacBean was Penn State’s top scorer in her last three seasons, tied with Payton Linnehan in 2023, leaving Penn State’s Aubrey Kulpa to lead the offensive forces this year.

Defenders Kayleigh Herr and Bella Ayscue will step up into larger roles as the tactical anchors and communication backbone this season to help bring together and lead their new lineup to a successful home opener Thursday and senior day Sunday.
